summary: Confirmed root cause of both defects. CLAUDE.md double-body: generate_claudemd() (merge.lua, called from init.lua load/unload -- the canonical, intentionally markerless computed-artifact regime per anchor commit bbed96afe) is correct; the stray duplicate is injected by sync.lua's reinject_loaded_extensions(), which still calls inject_section() for the claudemd merge key on every 'Load Core'/'Sync all' run. Fix: remove that per-extension inject_section() call and replace with one post-loop call to merge_mod.generate_claudemd(project_dir, config), mirroring the existing generate_opencode_json() precedent in the same function -- fixes OPENCODE.md's identical latent risk for free. Restoring section markers (the task's alternate option) is NOT recommended: three of four consuming call sites already assume no-markers. settings.json duplicate Stop hook: deep_merge's array dedup in merge.lua is whole-item vim.deep_equal, not matcher-aware, so merge-sources/settings-hooks.json's separately-declared claude-stop-notify.sh matcher block never matches the differently-shaped bundled block already in target settings.json (confirmed by the core manifest's own _comment, which predicts exactly this). Fix: one-time cleanup of deployed settings.json plus a matcher-aware merge for {matcher,hooks}-shaped arrays in deep_merge/merge_settings.
decisions_made: Do not restore <!-- SECTION: id --> markers to generate_claudemd() -- the no-markers computed-artifact model is a deliberate, already-adopted design (anchor commit bbed96afe), confirmed consistent across init.lua and verify.lua

Fix confined to sync.lua's reinject_loaded_extensions(): drop the per-extension inject_section() call for the config-markdown merge key, add one unconditional merge_mod.generate_claudemd(project_dir, config) call after the loop

settings.json dedup fix targets deep_merge/merge_settings in merge.lua with matcher-aware merging for {matcher,hooks}-shaped arrays, gated narrowly so non-hook arrays (permissions.allow, mcpServers) are unaffected

CLAUDE.md's current live state (897 lines, single copy) is a self-healing artifact of Engine A's full-overwrite regeneration, not evidence the bug is already fixed -- the next 'Load Core'/'Sync all' run would reintroduce it without the code fix
